sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: VIGOROUS SHORTWAVE TROUGH NOW MOVING INTO THE CNTRL INTERMOUNTAIN REGION WILL AMPLIFY A LITTLE FURTHER BEFORE ADVANCING EWD THROUGH THE CNTRL/NRN PLAINS AND UPPER MS VALLEY FRIDAY AND FRIDAY NIGHT. IN RESPONSE TO STRONG AGEOSTROPHIC FORCING ATTENDING AN UPPER JET ROTATING THROUGH BASE OF THE TROUGH...A LEE CYCLONE WILL DEEPEN AND LIFT NEWD THROUGH THE CNTRL PLAINS. BY EARLY EVENING THE LOW IS FORECAST TO BE OVER NERN NEB OR SERN SD WITH A TRAILING COLD FRONT SURGING SEWD THROUGH KS AND NWRN OK. A WARM FRONT WILL EXTEND EWD FROM THE LOW THROUGH THE UPPER MS VALLEY AND GREAT LAKES. A RESIDUAL CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WILL LIKELY LIFT NWD THROUGH CNTRL/NRN IA.

sections.title: MID-UPPER MS VALLEY REGION
sections.text: ONGOING MCS OVER IA DRIVEN PRIMARILY BY ISENTROPIC ASCENT ON THE NOSE OF A STRONG SLY LLJ WILL LIKELY PERSIST INTO FRIDAY MORNING OVER THE UPPER MS VALLEY REGION. THIS ACTIVITY WILL SHIFT NEWD AND WEAKEN AS WARMER AIR ALOFT LIFTS NEWD AND CAPS THE BOUNDARY LAYER TO SFC BASED STORMS DURING MUCH OF THE AFTERNOON. REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WILL PERSIST AND GRADUALLY MOVE NWD THROUGH IA AS 50 KT LLJ MIGRATES NNEWD THROUGH WARM SECTOR IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE DEVELOPING CYCLONE. RICH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE WITH UPPER 60S DEWPOINTS RESIDING OVER THE MIDDLE MS VALLEY WILL ADVECT NWD THROUGH WARM SECTOR INCLUDING MUCH OF ERN NEB INTO IA AND POSSIBLY EXTREME SRN MN BENEATH REMNANT EML PLUME...LIKELY RESULTING IN A CORRIDOR OF 1500-2000 J/KG MLCAPE. AS LLJ DEVELOPS NWD WITHIN DIVERGENT UPPER JET EXIT REGION...STORMS MAY INITIATE WITHIN ZONE OF ISENTROPIC ASCENT ALONG AND NORTH OF MODIFYING OUTFLOW BOUNDARY BY LATE AFTERNOON OR EARLY EVENING. PROVIDED MORNING STORMS DIMINISH...SUFFICIENT BOUNDARY LAYER RECOVERY MAY OCCUR TO SUPPORT SURFACE BASED STORMS. THIS ACTIVITY WILL EXIST WITHIN A VERY FAVORABLE KINEMATIC ENVIRONMENT WHERE NEAR SFC WINDS WILL BE BACKED TO ESELY BENEATH A STRONG LLJ RESULTING

sections.title: CNTRL THROUGH SRN PLAINS
sections.text: THE PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR WILL LIKELY BECOME MODERATELY TO STRONGLY UNSTABLE /2000-2500 J/KG MLCAPE/ AS REMNANT EML PLUME ADVECTS EWD ABOVE RICH LOW-LEVEL MOISTURE. HOWEVER...THIS WARM SECTOR WILL LIKELY REMAIN CAPPED TO SFC BASED STORMS UNTIL LATE AFTERNOON WHEN STRONG FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL ACCOMPANY THE SEWD SURGING COLD FRONT. GIVEN THE STRONG AND LINEAR NATURE OF THE FORCING...A RAPID UPSCALE GROWTH INTO LINES IS EXPECTED...BUT VERTICAL SHEAR WILL SUPPORT SOME ORGANIZED STRUCTURES WITHIN THE LINE INCLUDING SUPERCELLS AND BOWING SEGMENTS. LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WIND WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS FROM LATE AFTERNOON INTO THE EVENING.

sections.title: CNTRL GULF COASTAL AREA
sections.text: LOW-LEVEL WINDS/SHEAR WILL UNDERGO A MODEST INCREASE AS TROPICAL STORM KAREN APPROACHES THE LA COAST LATE FRIDAY NIGHT. A LIMITED RISK FOR ISOLATED TORNADOES EXIST AS THE OUTER RAIN BANDS NE OF THE CENTER MOVE INLAND. AT THIS TIME IT APPEARS GREATER TORNADO THREAT WILL BE DELAYED UNTIL THE DAY 2 PERIOD WHEN KAREN MOVES CLOSER TO THE COAST. SEE LATEST NHC DISCUSSIONS FOR MORE INFORMATION ON KAREN. ..DIAL/SMITH.. 10/04/2013

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: IN MID-UPPER LEVELS...PRIMARY MIDLATITUDE FEATURE FOR THIS FCST WILL BE LARGE CYCLONE CURRENTLY COVERING MUCH OF ROCKY MOUNTAIN REGION...AND CENTERED OVER SWRN WY/NERN UT AREA. ACCOMPANYING 500-MB LOW IS FCST TO REACH WRN PORTIONS NEB SANDHILLS BY 00Z...AND SERN SD BY END OF PERIOD...BY WHICH TIME POSITIVELY TILTED SHORTWAVE TROUGH WILL EXTEND SWWD ACROSS CO TO NRN AZ. AT SFC...11Z ANALYSIS SHOWED MAIN SFC CYCLONE OVER NERN KS...FCST TO DEEPEN CONSIDERABLY AS IT MOVES NEWD ACROSS CENTRAL NEB TODAY. THIS LOW SHOULD OCCLUDE OVER N-CENTRAL NEB THIS AFTN...WITH OCCLUDED FRONT EXTENDING EWD OR ESEWD TO TRIPLE POINT OVER NERN NEB/NWRN IA...WHERE SECONDARY LOW SHOULD FORM BY AROUND 00Z. TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL MOVE SEWD ACROSS NEB...KS...TX PANHANDLE AND WRN OK THROUGH EVENING. WARM FRONT ALREADY IS...AND WILL REMAIN...HEAVILY MODULATED BY OUTFLOW AND PRECIP OVER SERN NEB AND IA...AND WILL MOVE NWD TOWARD MN/IA BORDER REGION THROUGH EVENING.

sections.title: MID-UPPER MS VALLEY REGION
sections.text: SCATTERED TO LOCALLY NUMEROUS TSTMS ARE FCST TO DEVELOP THIS AFTN INVOF SFC LOW...AND ALONG NEARBY SEGMENTS OF COLD FRONT AND NEWD-RETREATING OUTFLOW/DIFFERENTIAL-HEATING BOUNDARY SERVING AS EFFECTIVE WARM FRONT. ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED CONVECTION ALSO MAY FORM IN NEARBY WARM SECTOR AWAY FROM THOSE BOUNDARIES...BUT THIS SCENARIO IS MORE CONDITIONAL GIVEN PRESENCE OF RESIDUAL EML-RELATED CINH. A FEW SUPERCELLS ARE POSSIBLE...OFFERING RISK OF TORNADOES...DAMAGING HAIL AND OCNL STG-SVR GUSTS. MOST INTENSE AND POTENTIALLY DAMAGING SVR THREAT IS EXPECTED TO BE RELATIVELY TIGHTLY FOCUSED INVOF THETAE GRADIENT RELATED TO RETREATING OUTFLOW/DIFFERENTIAL-HEATING BOUNDARY...FOR ANY RELATIVELY DISCRETE STORMS EITHER MOVING OUT OF WARM SECTOR OR OFF OF FRONT BEFORE TOO MUCH CONVECTIVE MERGER/INTERACTION OCCURS. REGIME OF BACKED LOW-LEVEL FLOW AND ENLARGED BOUNDARY-LAYER HODOGRAPHS WILL EXIST E AND NE OF APCHG SFC LOW. TIME SERIES OF FCST SOUNDINGS SUGGESTS 2-3 HOUR TIME WINDOW MID-LATE AFTN WHEN 200-400 J/KG OF 0-1 KM SRH MAY OVERLAP NRN FRINGES OF MID-UPPER 60S SFC DEW POINTS...STG HEATING...AND RELATED 1500-3000 J/KG MLCAPE. THIS OVERLAP WOULD OCCUR AROUND RETREATING BOUNDARY. LOWER BUT

sections.title: CENTRAL/SRN PLAINS
sections.text: SCATTERED TSTMS IN BANDS AND CLUSTERS SHOULD FORM INVOF SFC FRONT THIS AFTN AND EVENING...BACKBUILDING ACROSS MUCH OF KS/OK TODAY AND POTENTIALLY AS FAR AS PARTS OF NWRN/W-CENTRAL TX TONIGHT. DAMAGING GUSTS AND SPORADIC LARGE HAIL ARE POSSIBLE. KS/OK ACTIVITY WILL HAVE ACCESS FOR LONGEST TIME TO MOST FAVORABLE THERMODYNAMIC ENVIRONMENT IN AFTN AND EVENING...ALONG WITH SOMEWHAT STRONGER WINDS ALOFT THAN LATER CONVECTION OVER TX. AS SUCH...UNCONDITIONAL SVR THREAT DIMINISHES FROM SRN OK SWWD. HOWEVER...AT LEAST ISOLATED SVR HAIL/GUSTS MAY OCCUR WITH LATER/OVERNIGHT ACTIVITY FROM CENTRAL OK TO W-CENTRAL TX. SW OF PROXIMAL INFLUENCE OF SFC CYCLONE AND STRONGEST RELATED ISALLOBARIC FORCING...WARM-SECTOR/PREFRONTAL SFC FLOW SHOULD BE MORE VEERED...UNDERLYING WINDS ALOFT THAT BEAR SUBSTANTIAL FRONT-PARALLEL COMPONENT. AS SUCH...DOMINANT STORM MODE SHOULD BE QUASI-LINEAR...AFTER BRIEF EARLY-STAGE PHASES OF MULTICELL OR MRGL SUPERCELL CHARACTERISTICS.

sections.title: CENTRAL GULF COAST/LOWER DELTA REGION -- LATE PERIOD
sections.text: NHC FCSTS INDICATE OUTERMOST CIRCULATION ENVELOPE OF KAREN CAN AFFECT PORTIONS SERN LA LATE TONIGHT. CONCURRENT INCREASE IN LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPH SIZE OVER OUTER NERN SECTOR OF THIS CYCLONE WOULD JUXTAPOSE WITH FAVORABLE LOW-LEVEL THETAE...GRADUALLY SUPPORTING POTENTIAL FOR ANY SUSTAINED/OUTER CONVECTION THAT DOES FORM TO BECOME SUPERCELLULAR. HOWEVER...SEVERAL FACTORS PRECLUDE MORE THAN MRGL/SUB-CATEGORICAL PROBABILITIES ATTM...INCLUDING OBSERVED/FCST ASYMMETRIES IN KINEMATIC STRUCTURE...UNCERTAINTIES OVER PROGGED TRACK TIMING/INTENSITY PER NHC DISCUSSIONS...MODE/EXTENT UNCERTAINTIES REGARDING OUTER CONVECTIVE FEATURES...AND LACK OF GREATER BUOYANCY INLAND DUE TO RELATIVE NOCTURNAL INSTABILITY MIN. REF LATEST NHC ADVISORIES -- E.G. WMO HEADER WTNT32 KNHC -- FOR LATEST GUIDANCE ON TS KAREN. ..EDWARDS/LEITMAN.. 10/04/2013

sections.title: NEB/IA/MN
sections.text: MORNING WATER VAPOR LOOPS SHOW A STRONG UPPER LOW OVER NORTHWEST CO...WITH MULTIPLE SHORTWAVE TROUGHS ROTATING THROUGH THE BASE OF THE LOW AND INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS. ONE SUCH TROUGH IS NOW OVER SOUTHEAST CO/SOUTHWEST KS AND IS EXPECTED TO TRACK INTO EASTERN NEB/KS BY EVENING. AT THE SURFACE...THE PRIMARY LOW IS ANALYZED OVER SOUTHERN NEB WITH A COLD FRONT EXTENDING SOUTHWESTWARD INTO THE OK PANHANDLE. THIS FRONT WILL MIX EASTWARD THROUGH THE DAY...LIKELY EXTENDING FROM SOUTHEAST NEB INTO EASTERN KS BY LATE AFTERNOON. THIS CORRIDOR WILL LIKELY SEE THE INITIATION OF STRONG/SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS. THE INITIAL STORMS SHOULD FORM NEAR THE TRIPLE POINT OVER EASTERN NEB AND TRACK INTO WESTERN IA DURING THE EARLY EVENING. DEEP LAYER SHEAR VECTORS PERPENDICULAR TO THE SURFACE BOUNDARY WILL PROMOTE DISCRETE CONVECTIVE MODE...WITH SUFFICIENT VERTICAL SHEAR FOR SUPERCELL STORMS. VERY LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES /POSSIBLY STRONG/ MAY OCCUR ACROSS THE MODERATE RISK AREA. STORMS MAY ORGANIZE INTO A BOWING LINE DURING THE EVENING WITH A CONTINUED SEVERE THREAT INTO SOUTHERN MN AND NORTHEAST IA.

sections.title: SOUTHERN IA THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: ANOTHER IMPORTANT SURFACE FEATURE IS A RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM MORNING CONVECTION THAT ARCS FROM SOUTHEAST NEB ACROSS NORTHWEST MO INTO SOUTHEAST IA. THIS BOUNDARY WILL LIKELY LIFT SLOWLY NORTHWARD AND WEAKEN TODAY...WITH SLOW EROSION OF CLOUD COVER AND DESTABILIZATION OCCURRING OVER SOUTHERN IA. DEPENDING ON THE EXTENT OF DESTABILIZATION...THIS REGION MAY BECOME QUITE FAVORABLE FOR SUPERCELL STORMS. BACKED LOW LEVEL WINDS... RESIDUAL LOW LEVEL MOISTURE /DEWPOINTS IN THE MID-UPPER 60S/...AND A WEAKENED CAPPING INVERSION MAY ENHANCE THE SEVERE RISK. THEREFORE HAVE SHIFTED THE MODERATE RISK AREA FARTHER SOUTH TO INCLUDE THIS REGION. IF DISCRETE STORMS FORM...VERY LARGE HAIL AND A FEW TORNADOES WOULD BE POSSIBLE.

sections.title: KS/MO/OK
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM ALONG THE COLD FRONT FROM CENTRAL KS INTO NORTHERN OK BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST SUFFICIENT CAP TO LIMIT THE POTENTIAL FOR DISCRETE STORMS AHEAD OF THE FRONT. THE MAIN RISK APPEARS TO BE A SQUALL LINE COINCIDENT WITH THE COLD FRONT...CAPABLE OF DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL FOR A FEW HOURS DURING THE EVENING. THIS ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY BEGIN TO WEAKEN BEFORE MIDNIGHT AS DIURNAL COOLING TAKES PLACE.

sections.title: SOUTHERN LA
sections.text: TS KAREN IS MOVING SLOWLY NORTHWARD ACROSS THE CENTRAL GULF OF MEXICO. IT APPEARS THAT SUBSTANTIAL STRENGTHENING OF LOW LEVEL WINDS FIELDS IN THE NORTHERN SEMICIRCLE OF THE CIRCULATION WILL NOT REACH SOUTHERN LA UNTIL VERY LATE TONIGHT. HAVE MAINTAINED THE LOW TORNADO PROBABILITIES IN THE CURRENT OUTLOOK...BUT THE RISK IS MORE LIKELY TO BE DELAYED UNTIL THE DAY2 PERIOD. ..HART/GRAMS.. 10/04/2013

sections.title: NEB/IA/MN
sections.text: RELATIVELY FEW CHANGES TO THE EXISTING OUTLOOK AND ASSOCIATED REASONING...SEE PRIOR DISCUSSION BELOW...TORNADO WATCH 539 AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS. WITH SURFACE BASED TSTMS LIKELY TO STEADILY INCREASE THROUGH LATE AFTERNOON ESPECIALLY NEAR/SOUTHEAST OF A SURFACE TRIPLE POINT...THE GREATEST OVERALL SEVERE THREAT AND TORNADO POTENTIAL /POSSIBLY STRONG/ IS STILL EXPECTED ACROSS FAR EASTERN NEB INTO WESTERN IA INCLUDING AREAS ALONG THE I-80 CORRIDOR. THIS IS IN VICINITY OF A WARM FRONT/RESIDUAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WHERE LOW-LEVEL SHEAR/SRH WILL BE MAXIMIZED.

sections.title: KS/MO/OK
sections.text: DEEPENING CU FIELD IS BECOMING READILY APPARENT IN VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY AT 20Z ACROSS EAST-CENTRAL/SOUTH-CENTRAL KS INTO NORTHWEST/FAR WESTERN OK. TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP/INCREASE THROUGH LATE AFTERNOON ALONG THE EAST-SOUTHEASTWARD ADVANCING COLD FRONT...WITH SOME ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT ALONG THE DRYLINE ACROSS NORTHWEST/WEST-CENTRAL OK. ESPECIALLY NEAR THE DRYLINE...SEMI-DISCRETE/POTENTIALLY SUPERCELLULAR DEVELOPMENT WILL BE POSSIBLE /INCLUDING HAIL AND PERHAPS SOME TORNADO RISK/ PRIOR TO THE DRYLINE GRADUALLY BEING OVERTAKEN /FROM NORTHWEST TO SOUTHEAST/ INTO THIS EVENING. ..GUYER.. 10/04/2013 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1126 AM CDT FRI OCT 04 2013/

sections.title: IA
sections.text: CLUSTER OF SUPERCELLS OVER NWRN IA THAT INITIATED ALONG AN ARCING COLD FRONT HAVE BEEN PROLIFIC TORNADO PRODUCERS ACROSS NERN NEB INTO EXTREME NWRN IA. THESE STORMS RESIDE ALONG AND JUST NORTH OF A CONSOLIDATED WARM FRONT/OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WHERE SFC WINDS ARE BACKED TO ELY ON NOSE OF A 40 KT LLJ RESULTING IN LARGE HODOGRAPHS WITH 300-400 M2/S2 0-1 KM STORM RELATIVE HELICITY. HOWEVER...THE STORMS IN NWRN IA HAVE BEGUN TO MERGE INTO CLUSTERS...AND THIS MAY TEND TO HAVE A NEGATIVE IMPACT ON MORE PROLIFIC FUTURE TORNADO PRODUCTION. NEVERTHELESS...ACTIVITY WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A RISK FOR LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WIND AND ISOLATED TORNADOES...SOME OF WHICH COULD BE STRONG THIS EVENING. FARTHER SOUTH DEVELOPMENT HAS BEEN MORE ISOLATED...POSSIBLY DUE TO EFFECTS OF NEWD ADVANCING MID-UPPER DRY SLOT TO THE EAST OF UPPER JET AXIS. HOWEVER...A FEW CELLS HAVE DEVELOPED ALONG THE EWD SURGING FRONT OVER SWRN IA AND LIFTING NEWD THROUGH THE UNSTABLE WARM SECTOR WHERE MLCAPE IS ON THE ORDER OF 2000 J/KG. GIVEN THE FAVORABLE KINEMATIC ENVIRONMENT...THIS ACTIVITY WILL CONTINUE TO POSE A RISK FOR ISOLATED TORNADOES AND LARGE HAIL AS THEY MOVE NEWD TOWARD CNTRL IA.

sections.title: ERN KS THROUGH CNTRL OK
sections.text: BROKEN LINE OF STORMS PERSISTS ALONG SEWD ADVANCING COLD FRONT FROM NERN KS SWWD THROUGH SWRN OK WHERE THE DRYLINE HAS BEEN THE INITIATING MECHANISM. EVENING RAOB DATA INDICATE THE PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR IS MODERATELY UNSTABLE WITH 1500-2000 J/KG MLCAPE. HOWEVER...A PRONOUNCED CAPPING INVERSION /ESPECIALLY EVIDENT ON THE OUN SOUNDING/ IS PRESENT IN THE WARM SECTOR SUGGESTING STORMS WILL REMAIN CONFINED TO ZONE OF LINEAR FORCING ALONG THE FRONT. ACTIVITY IS EMBEDDED WITHIN 40-50 KT EFFECTIVE SHEAR...AND A FEW NEWD ADVANCING EMBEDDED BOWING SEGMENTS AS WELL AS SOME SUPERCELL CHARACTERISTICS ARE POSSIBLE AS ACTIVITY DEVELOPS SEWD OVERNIGHT. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND STRONG TO DAMAGING WIND GUSTS WILL BE THE MAIN THREATS THIS EVENING. ..DIAL.. 10/05/2013

mesoscale_discussions.summary: WIDESPREAD/LOCALLY VIGOROUS STORMS CONTINUE MOVING ACROSS IA AND VICINITY. THE STRONGEST OF THE CELLS -- NOW CROSSING SERN IA -- WILL REMAIN CAPABLE OF LOCALLY GUSTY/DAMAGING WINDS AND MARGINAL HAIL. HOWEVER...IT APPEARS ATTM THAT THREAT WILL REMAIN ISOLATED ENOUGH TO NEGATE THE NEED FOR A WW.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STORMS CONTINUE TO DEVELOP/MOVE ENEWD ACROSS THE IA VICINITY THIS MORNING...NEAR AND JUST N OF A SURFACE WARM FRONT EXTENDING ACROSS SRN IA. THE STORMS ARE BEING SUPPORTED BY CONTINUED ISENTROPIC ASCENT...WITH A SWLY LOW-LEVEL JET ASCENDING ATOP A RELATIVELY COOL/STABLE BOUNDARY LAYER. WITH MORNING TOP AND DVN RAOBS REVEALING RELATIVELY STEEP LAPSE RATES/MODERATE BUOYANCY ATOP THE STABLE LAYER ALONG WITH MID-LEVEL FLOW NEAR 50 KT...THREAT FOR A COUPLE OF STRONGER/ROTATING CELLS AND ATTENDANT SEVERE THREAT CONTINUES. HAVING SAID THAT...MODEL FORECASTS SUPPORT THE TYPICAL DIURNAL DECREASE IN THE LOW-LEVEL JET OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS...AND THUS ANY MARKED INCREASE IN COVERAGE/INTENSITY OF STORMS APPEARS UNLIKELY. THE LATEST HIGH-RES CONVECTION-ALLOWING GUIDANCE ALSO CONFIRMS THIS CONCLUSION...WITH ALL RUNS SHOWING A STEADY DECREASE IN CONVECTION THROUGH MIDDAY. THEREFORE -- WHILE SHORT-TERM/ISOLATED SEVERE RISK WILL CONTINUE...THE EXPECTED/GRADUAL DECREASE SHOULD PRECLUDE THE NEED FOR WW ISSUANCE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ONGOING EVOLUTION OF THE ENVIRONMENT INVOF THE MID MO VALLEY CONTINUES TO SUGGEST SLOWLY INCREASING SEVERE RISK. WW ISSUANCE WILL LIKELY BE REQUIRED IN THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS AS SEVERE POTENTIAL -- INCLUDING THE RISK FOR A FEW TORNADOES -- EVOLVES.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: LATEST VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS LITTLE IN THE WAY OF SURFACE-BASED CU DEVELOPMENT IN PROXIMITY TO THE SURFACE LOW OVER CENTRAL NEB AND ASSOCIATED/ATTENDANT COLD/WARM FRONTS. AN 18Z RAOB FROM TOP INDICATES THAT CAPPING REMAINS IN PLACE...THOUGH HEATING/MIXING WILL CONTINUE TO ERODE THE INVERSION WITH TIME -- AIDED BY ASCENT INVOF THE SURFACE SYSTEM. ATTM...GREATEST RISK FOR INITIAL DEVELOPMENT APPEARS TO EXIST OVER SERN NEB AND NERN KS -- I.E. JUST SOUTHEAST OF THE SURFACE LOW -- SOMETIME WITHIN THE NEXT 1-2 HOURS. AS HEATING OF THE MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER INTO THE LOW TO MID 80S SUPPORTS MIXED-LAYER CAPE NOW INTO THE 1000 TO 2000 J/KG RANGE...VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS SHOULD EVOLVE RATHER QUICKLY AFTER INITIAL ONSET OF DEEP CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT. ORGANIZATION WILL BE AIDED BY A FAVORABLY STRONG DEEP-LAYER WIND FIELD FEATURING FLOW THAT VEERS MARKEDLY WITH HEIGHT -- PARTICULARLY NEAR AND TO THE COOL SIDE OF THE WARM FRONT EXTENDING ESEWD ACROSS FAR SERN NEB AND THE NRN TIER OF NWRN MO COUNTIES. ALONG WITH AN EVENTUAL RISK FOR LARGE HAIL AND LOCALLY DAMAGING WINDS...THE RISK FOR A FEW TORNADOES IS ALSO APPARENT -- PARTICULARLY WITH STORMS DEVELOPING IN THE ZONE OF STRONGEST LOW-LEVEL SHEAR INVOF THE WARM FRONT.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR DMGG WINDS AND LARGE HAIL...AND PERHAPS A TORNADO...WILL INCREASE THROUGH THE LATE AFTERNOON. TRENDS ARE BEING MONITORED FOR SIGNS OF CONVECTIVE INITIATION...WHICH WILL LIKELY NECESSITATE WATCH ISSUANCE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: SFC ANALYSIS FROM 19Z SHOWS A DRYLINE/COLD FRONT INTERSECTION NEAR PTT...WITH THE DRYLINE EXTENDING SWWD INTO THE ERN TX PANHANDLE...AND A COLD FRONT ARCING WSWWD ACROSS SWRN KS INTO THE NRN TX PANHANDLE. MORE RECENTLY...VISIBLE SATELLITE TRENDS HAVE SHOWED BOUNDARY LAYER-BASED CU INCREASING ALONG THE DRYLINE...BUT LATEST OBJECTIVE ANALYSIS FIELDS SUGGEST NOTABLE MLCINH IS STILL PRESENT. GIVEN ADDITIONAL SFC HEATING /WITH CONVECTIVE TEMPERATURES NEAR 88-90 F PER RAP/NAM FORECAST SOUNDINGS/...AND WEAK BUT PERSISTENT LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE ALONG THE DRYLINE...REMAINING MLCINH SHOULD CONTINUE TO WEAKEN AND RESULT IN CONVECTIVE INITIATION...POSSIBLY BY 21Z. RECENT SUITE OF HIGH-RESOLUTION NUMERICAL GUIDANCE SUGGESTS TSTM DEVELOPMENT WILL OCCUR ALONG THE DRYLINE INITIALLY OVER WRN OK INTO FAR SRN KS...AND ALONG THE COLD FRONT INTO CNTRL KS. VEERING VERTICAL WIND PROFILES YIELDING EFFECTIVE SHEAR VALUES OF 40-50 KT WILL SUPPORT SUPERCELL STRUCTURES WITH ANY SUSTAINED DISCRETE STORMS THAT CAN DEVELOP...CAPABLE OF PRODUCING LARGE HAIL...DMGG WIND GUSTS...AND PERHAPS A TORNADO. HOWEVER...THE TEMPORAL WINDOW FOR DISCRETE CONVECTION REMAINS UNCERTAIN...AS THE COLD FRONT IS FORECAST TO ACCELERATE SWD LATER THIS EVENING AND WILL LIKELY UNDERCUT TSTMS WITHIN THE WARM SECTOR...WITH THE DOMINANT MODE EVENTUALLY TRANSITIONING TO A LINE.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE TORNADO THREAT APPEARS LIKELY TO CONTINUE ACROSS NE NEB INTO THE EARLY EVENING AND MAY SPREAD NWD INTO SE SD AND POSSIBLY EWD INTO NW IA. ISOLATED LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WILL ALSO BE POSSIBLE WITH THE MORE INTENSE STORMS. A LOCAL EXTENSION HAS BEEN DONE ACROSS SERN SD FROM WEST OF YANKTON SD EWD INTO NW IA.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THE LATEST SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS A 1001 MB LOW IN NERN NEB WITH A MOIST AXIS EXTENDING FROM NEAR THE SFC LOW SEWD ACROSS THE OMAHA AREA WHERE SFC DEWPOINTS ARE IN THE MID 60S TO LOWER 70S F. THIS IS CONTRIBUTING TO MLCAPE IN THE 2000 TO 2500 J/KG RANGE AS ESTIMATED BY MESOSCALE ANALYSIS. IN ADDITION...THE OMAHA AND SIOUX FALLS WSR-88D VWPS SHOW DEEP LAYER SHEAR AROUND 60 KT WITH 0-1 KM SHEAR OF 25 TO 30 KT. THIS MAGNITUDE OF INSTABILITY AND SHEAR SHOULD CONTINUE TO SUPPORT SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT AND TORNADOES WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE MORE DOMINANT ROTATING STORMS. THE CELLS IN NERN NEB JUST TO THE SOUTH OF THE SD BORDER ARE SFC-BASED AND SHOULD REMAIN SO FOR SEVERAL MORE HOURS BEFORE MOVING INTO THE COOLER AIR IN THE SIOUX FALLS AREA. FOR THIS REASON...THE STORMS SHOULD CONTINUE TO HAVE A TORNADO THREAT INTO EARLY THIS EVENING. IN ADDITION TO THE TORNADO THREAT...ISOLATED LARGE HAIL WILL BE POSSIBLE DUE TO THE COLD TEMPS ALOFT AND MODERATE INSTABILITY IN PLACE. AS THE STORMS CONTINUE TO EXPAND IN COVERAGE...LINEAR DEVELOPMENT WILL BE POSSIBLE ALONG THE FRONT SUGGESTING THE WIND DAMAGE THREAT COULD INCREASE EARLY THIS EVENING.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE GREATEST THREAT FOR LARGE HAIL/STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL PROBABLY OCCUR OVER PORTIONS OF W-CNTRL AND NWRN OK WITH CELLULAR STORMS THAT DEVELOP AND MOVE NNE AND RESIDE LONGEST IN THE OPEN SECTOR AHEAD OF THE FRONT.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RADAR/VISIBLE SATELLITE IMAGERY SHOWS A NNE-SSW ORIENTED FRONT ACROSS NERN INTO S-CNTRL KS THEN ARCING SWWD INTO THE NRN TX PANHANDLE. A DRYLINE IS DRAPED FROM NEAR THE OK-TX BORDER NNE TO WHERE IT INTERSECTS THE FRONT IN NWRN OK. A RESERVOIR OF MID 60S DEWPOINTS RESIDES AHEAD OF THESE BOUNDARIES OVER OK AND HAS LED TO UPWARDS OF 2300 J/KG MLCAPE WHEN MODIFYING THE 18Z LMN RAOB FOR CURRENT SURFACE CONDITIONS AND IS MORE UNSTABLE THAN OBJECTIVE RAP GUIDANCE INDICATES. KVNX AND KFDR HODOGRAPH SIZE --WHEN INPUT WITH OBSERVED STORM MOTIONS-- IS YIELDING LESS THAN 100 M2/S2 0-3 KM SRH AND THIS IMPLIES ONLY A LIMITED/MARGINAL TORNADO THREAT FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS. THE MAIN SEVERE THREAT WILL LIKELY BE ASSOCIATED STORMS THAT CAN DEVELOP NEAR THE DRYLINE OVER W-CNTRL OK AND MOVE NEWD INTO N-CNTRL OK DURING THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS AHEAD OF THE FRONT. FARTHER N OVER FAR NWRN OK AND INTO S-CNTRL KS...STORM MOTIONS WILL TEND TO RESULT IN STORMS GETTING UNDERCUT BY THE FRONT AND LEADING TO UPSCALE GROWTH OF INITIALLY CELLULAR ACTIVITY INTO A CONVECTIVE LINE THIS EVENING. AN INITIAL LARGE HAIL THREAT MAY ACCOMPANY THE STRONGER UPDRAFTS BUT THE THREAT WILL PROBABLY TRANSITION THIS EVENING TO MAINLY AN ISOLD STRONG TO LOCALLY SEVERE WIND GUST RISK. ..SMITH.. 10/04/2013 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT MAY CONTINUE FROM SWRN OK NEWD INTO ERN KS AND NW MO LATE THIS EVENING. HAIL AND MARGINALLY SEVERE WIND GUSTS WILL BE POSSIBLE WITH THE STRONGER CELLS. WW ISSUANCE IS NOT ANTICIPATED AFTER THE 03Z EXPIRATION OF WW 540. A LOCAL EXTENSION COULD BECOME NECESSARY ACROSS THE SRN PART OF WW 540 WHERE THE SEVERE THREAT COULD LAST A BIT LONGER.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A BROKEN LINE OF STRONG THUNDERSTORMS IS ONGOING FROM NEAR KANSAS CITY SWWD INTO WRN OK ALONG A COLD FRONT. THE ACTIVITY IS BEING SUPPORTED BY LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE ALONG THE FRONT. SFC DEWPOINTS AHEAD OF THE BOUNDARY ARE IN THE MID TO UPPER 60S F WITH MESOSCALE ANALYSIS SHOWING MODERATE INSTABILITY WITH MLCAPE IN THE 1000 TO 2000 J/KG RANGE. THIS COMBINED WITH 35 TO 45 KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR EVIDENT ON WSR-88D VWPS SHOULD BE ENOUGH TO CONTINUE AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT FOR A FEW MORE HOURS. ALTHOUGH HAIL AND A FEW MARGINALLY SEVERE WIND GUSTS COULD OCCUR ESPECIALLY IN WCNTRL OK...THE THREAT SHOULD CONTINUE TO GRADUALLY DECREASE AS DESTABILIZATION OCCURS LATE THIS EVENING INTO THE OVERNIGHT PERIOD.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: AN ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT MAY CONTINUE INTO THE OVERNIGHT PERIOD ACROSS FAR SRN MN AND NCNTRL IA REACHING SWRN WI AROUND MIDNIGHT. LARGE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE WILL BE THE PRIMARY THREATS. GENERAL DOWNWARD TRENDS SUGGEST THAT A NEW WW WILL NOT BE NECESSARY.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: A CLUSTER OF STRONG TO SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS IS ONGOING NEAR THE MN-IA STATELINE. THIS ACTIVITY IS LOCATED ALONG A SHARPLY DEFINED WARM FRONT EXTENDING FROM THE SIOUX FALLS AREA EWD INTO NERN IA. SFC DEWPOINTS NEAR OF THE BOUNDARY ARE IN THE MID 60S F WITH MLCAPE ESTIMATED FROM 1000 TO 2000 J/KG. THE INSTABILITY ALONG WITH LIFT ASSOCIATED WITH A 40 TO 45 KT LOW-LEVEL JET SHOULD SUPPORT CONVECTIVE DEVELOPMENT INTO THE OVERNIGHT PERIOD. THE LACROSSE WI WSR-88D VWP SHOWS 55 KT OF 0-6 KM SHEAR WITH ENOUGH LOW-LEVEL SHEAR FOR A CONTINUED SEVERE THREAT. HOWEVER...THE POTENTIAL FOR ORGANIZED STORMS IS EXPECTED TO BECOME MORE ISOLATED WITH TIME OVER THE NEXT FEW HOURS WITH MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL AND WIND DAMAGE POSSIBLE OVERNIGHT.
